tagline: Straight north across the grain country to the breaks.
intro: From US 40 at Sharon Springs, K-27 runs north 88 miles across grain country and over the creeks, through Goodland at I-70 and on through St. Francis to the Nebraska line. It is the westernmost north-south state highway in Kansas, never far from Colorado.

Near the top of the state the flat gives way. The Arikaree Breaks are a band of badlands two to three miles wide, cut by water into loess that lies as much as 100 feet thick, all ravines and vertical cliffs.

moments.title: Sharon Springs
moments.text: Founded in 1868 as Eagle Tail station and renamed in 1886 for Sharon Springs, New York, and in 2013 the largest sinkhole in Kansas opened just north of town.

moments.title: Goodland
moments.text: Laid out in 1887 to settle a four-way quarrel over the county seat, it won the vote, and in January 1888 an armed party from Goodland went to Eustis and took the records.

moments.title: Arikaree Breaks
moments.text: North of St. Francis, water has carved the loess into ravines and cliffs that run on into Colorado and Nebraska, reached only by unpaved back roads.

practical: The Arikaree Breaks are on private land, reached only on unpaved roads; stay out of fenced areas.
